answer: Because the vertex index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the anchor audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the delta identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 182 runs and collects one. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 182 answers need 182 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
